ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of the square $ABCD$ is $4$, and the point $P$ is on the diagonal $AC$ (not including endpoints). With $PA$ and $PB$ as adjacent sides, a square $PAQB$ is formed. What is the minimum value of the diagonal length $PQ$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, let AB and PQ intersect at point O, and draw $OE\perp AC$ through point $O$, \\
since quadrilateral $AQBP$ is a parallelogram, \\
therefore $AO=OB=\frac{1}{2}AB=2$, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square, \\
therefore $\angle AOE=\angle OAE=45^\circ$, \\
thus, OE=AE, \\
therefore $OE^{2}+AE^{2}=AO^{2}$, \\
thus, OE=$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AO$, \\
according to the problem, $P$ is a moving point on $AC$, when point P coincides with point E, PO reaches its minimum value. \\
At this time, $PQ=2OE=2\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AO=\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}$.

method.method_draft: Coordinate/vector optimization route: First read the diagram as a square ABCD with AB vertical, BC horizontal, diagonal AC, and P on AC; the constructed quadrilateral AQBP has P and Q as opposite vertices and AB as the other diagonal. Set coordinates A=(0,0), B=(0,-4), C=(4,-4), D=(4,0). Then AC has equation P=(t,-t) for 0<t<4. Because AQBP is a parallelogram/square, the midpoint of PQ equals the midpoint of AB, namely O=(0,-2), so Q=2O-P=(-t,-4+t). Then PQ=2OP=2√(t^2+(2-t)^2). raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the side length of the square $ABCD$ is $4$, and the point $P$ is on the diagonal $AC$ (not including endpoints). With $PA$ and $PB$ as adjacent sides, a square $PAQB$ is formed. What is the minimum value of the diagonal length $PQ$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, let AB and PQ intersect at point O, and draw $OE\perp AC$ through point $O$, \\
since quadrilateral $AQBP$ is a parallelogram, \\
therefore $AO=OB=\frac{1}{2}AB=2$, \\
since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a square, \\
therefore $\angle AOE=\angle OAE=45^\circ$, \\
thus, OE=AE, \\
therefore $OE^{2}+AE^{2}=AO^{2}$, \\
thus, OE=$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AO$, \\
according to the problem, $P$ is a moving point on $AC$, when point P coincides with point E, PO reaches its minimum value. \\
At this time, $PQ=2OE=2\times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}AO=\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}$
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, ABCD is a square, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; diagonal AC has been drawn, and point P is located on diagonal AC; there is point Q on the left side, and quadrilateral A-Q-B-P is drawn, while segment PQ intersects side AB. Reasoning: Let the intersection point of PQ and AB be O. From the constructed quadrilateral AQBP being a parallelogram, its diagonals AB and PQ bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of AB and also the midpoint of PQ. The side length AB of square ABCD is 4, therefore AO=OB=2, and PQ=2OP. When point P moves on line AC, the minimum value of OP equals the perpendicular distance from point O to line AC; let the foot of the perpendicular be E, then the minimum OP=OE. Because ABCD is a square, AC and AB form 45°, so triangle AOE is a 45°-45°-90° right triangle, and the hypotenuse AO=2. Therefore OE=AO/√2=2/√2=√2. Thus the minimum value of PQ is 2OE=2√2.
